subject.event: Self-reported elevated stress in the coming week
subject.outcomeDefinition: The user records stress >= 4 (on the 1-5 DailyCheckIn scale) on at least 3 of the 7 daily check-ins dated 2026-06-06 through 2026-06-12.
subject.resolutionSource: DailyCheckIn.stress rows for this user, which are user-entered and are not produced by the risk engine.

reasons.detail: Five tracked days against the engine's 28-day full window. Below MIN_BASELINE_DAYS (7), so computeMetricBaseline returns null for every metric.

Four of five scoring dimensions are inactive. The engine would renormalize weights over the single active dimension, producing a score that describes check-ins alone while presenting as an overall risk.
With no personal baseline, every subscore would be judged against nothing. This user's own normal is what the product compares against, and it does not exist yet.

baseline.reason: No personal baseline exists yet. computeMetricBaseline returns null below MIN_BASELINE_DAYS (7), and this user has 5 tracked days, so all five metric baselines are null.

sampleSize.basis: Days since signup with any logged metric. The engine's fullTrackedDays is 28.

criticalMissing: Four of five scoring dimensions are inactive: no sleep records, no exercise records, no calendar integration, no work sessions. Only DailyCheckIn is populated.
No personal baseline for any metric, so every subscore is judged against nothing.

outliers.handling: With 5 observations outlier detection has no power; the result should be given no weight.

regime.description: User onboarded 5 days ago; no schedule changes recorded.

market.reason: No market or external reference expectation exists for an individual's self-reported stress.
